THE LANDING CAUGHT A DEFECT THE BRANCH COULD NOT SEE: tests/test-apex-trust-enforcement.sh was 77/77 in the agent's worktree and went 73/1 on the first clean checkout, failing its own first assertion - 'no pinned Fulcio root at files/system/trust/fulcio-root.pem, every update would be refused'. Cause: .gitignore line 13 carries *.pem under 'Signing material - PRIVATE KEYS NEVER IN REPO', and it silently matched the PUBLIC Sigstore root the verifier needs. git add said nothing, git status showed a clean tree, and the suite passed because the file existed UNTRACKED in the worktree that wrote it. Severity is the point: under the shipped default (signature=enforce) a missing root is CouldNotRun, and CouldNotRun REFUSES - so the omission would not have broken a feature, it would have stopped every machine in the fleet from updating, shipped by a rule written to prevent leaking a private key. Fixed by negating the ignore BY EXACT PATH (not by directory, so the next .pem there is a decision) and committing the anchor after checking the bytes rather than assuming them: self-signed, subject and issuer both O=sigstore.dev CN=sigstore, valid 2021-10-07 to 2031-10-05, SHA-256 fingerprint 3B:A7:B6:CC:4E:95:46:9D:4D:33:4B:49:CB:25:7A:D8:53:70:76:FA:84:B0:CA:87:FF:4E:CF:E6:A5:46:80:C1, byte-identical to the value Containerfile.base pins and fails the build over. VERIFIED ON THE LANDED TIP: test-apex-trust-enforcement 77/0 (from 73/1), cargo test --locked --workspace --no-fail-fast 2040 passed / 0 failed across 30 binaries, test-apex-trust 6/0 structural, test-apex-verbs 44/0, test-apex-channel 22/0, test-apex-host 52/0, check-doc-verbs on docs/trust-enforcement.md 2 valid, run-clippy PASS in the container, no conflict markers.

_field_contract: resume.sh does os.path.isdir(worktree) and git rev-list origin/<branch>..HEAD, so `worktree` and `branch` must each be ONE value. An agent working two repos records the other in second_worktree/second_branch, which resume.sh ignores. Writing 'a and b' there makes the next report say 'no worktree' for a worktree that is fine.
